questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ is released from rest in a uniform electric field. If there is no other force on the particle, the dependence of its speed $v$ on the distance $x$ travelled by it is correctly given by (graphs are schematic and not drawn to scale)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The particle is at rest initially.

So, the initial velocity& $u = 0ms^{- 1}$.

The force on the charged particle in the uniform electric field,

$F = qE$

$⇒ ma = qE$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{qE}{m}$

Applying the velocity-displacement equation under constant acceleration,

$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2ax$

$⇒ v^{2} = {0}^{2} + 2\left(\dfrac{qE}{m}\right)x$

$⇒ v^{2} = \dfrac{2qE}{m}x$

questions.q: A ball is thrown up with a certain velocity so that it reaches a height $h .$ Find the ratio of the two different times of the ball reaching $\dfrac{h}{3}$ in both the directions.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$u = \sqrt{2gh}$
Now,

$S = \dfrac{h}{3}, a = - g$

$S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$
$\dfrac{h}{3} = \sqrt{2gh}t + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(- g\right)t^{2}$
$t^{2}\left(\dfrac{g}{2}\right) - \sqrt{2gh}t + \dfrac{h}{3} = 0$

From quadratic equation

${t}_{1}, {t}_{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh} \pm \sqrt{2gh - \dfrac{4g}{2}\dfrac{h}{3}}}{g}$

$\dfrac{t1}{t2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh} - \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}}{\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}}$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Consider a small steel ball as shown below:

As shown in diagram, buoyancy force ${F}_{B} = F$.

Applying Newton's second law, we get

$mg - {F}_{B} - {F}_{v} = ma$

$⇒ \left(ρ\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right)g - \left({ρ}_{L}\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right)g - 6\piηrv = m\dfrac{dv}{dt}$

Let $\dfrac{4}{3m}\piR^{3}g\left(ρ - {ρ}_{L}\right) = {K}_{1}$ and $\dfrac{6\piηr}{m} = {K}_{2}$, then we get

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = {K}_{1} - {K}_{2}v$

Integrating both sides, we get

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{{K}_{1} - {K}_{2}v} = {∫}_{0}^{t}dt$

$⇒ - \dfrac{1}{K2}ln{\left[{K}_{1} - {K}_{2}v\right]0}^{v} = t$

$⇒ \ln \left(\dfrac{{K}_{1} - {K}_{2}v}{K1}\right) = - {K}_{2}t$

$⇒ {K}_{1} - {K}_{2}v = {K}_{1}e^{- {K}_{2}t}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{K1}{K2} \left[1 - e^{- {K}_{2}t}\right]

Clearly, option B matches with the given variation of velocity with time.

$

questions.q: Two buses $P$~and $Q$ start from a point at the same time and move in a straight line and their positions are represented by ${x}_{P}\left(t\right) = \alphat + \betat^{2}$ and ${x}_{Q}\left(t\right) = ft - t^{2}$. At what time, both the buses have same velocity ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,& $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Given,~${x}_{P}\left(t\right) = \alphat + \betat^{2}$

Velocity of bus~$P$~is~${v}_{P} = \dfrac{d{x}_{P}}{dt} = \alpha + 2\betat$~and velocity of bus~$Q$~is ${v}_{Q} = f - 2t$

When~${v}_{P} = {v}_{Q}$

$⇒ \alpha + 2\betat = f - 2t$

~$⇒ f - \alpha = 2\left(\beta + 1\right)t ⇒ t = \dfrac{f - \alpha}{2\left(\beta + 1\right)}$

questions.q: An object moves with speed ${v}_{1}, {v}_{2}\text{and}{v}_{3}$ along a line segment $AB, BC\text{and}CD$ respectively as shown in figure. Where $AB = BC\text{and}AD = 3AB$, then average speed of the object will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Speed of an object is defined as the distance travelled by the object per unit time.

Let's assume that,& $AB = d$. So,~$BC = d, AD = 3d$. Also, assume that the time required by the object to travel~$AB, BC, CD$~are~${t}_{1}, {t}_{2}, {t}_{3}$~respectively.

Now,

$\begin{cases}AD & = & 3AB \\ AB + BC + CD & = & 3AB \\ AB + AB + CD & = & 3AB \\ CD & = & AB\end{cases}$

Hence,

$\begin{cases}{t}_{1} & = & \dfrac{AB}{v1} \\ & = & \dfrac{d}{v1} \\ {t}_{2} & = & \dfrac{d}{v2} \\ {t}_{3} & = & \dfrac{d}{v3}\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the average speed~ \left({v}_{a}\right)$~of the object is given by

${v}_{a} = \dfrac{AD}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2} + {t}_{3}} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Substitute the expressions for the parameters into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the required average speed of the object.

$\begin{cases}{v}_{a} & = & \dfrac{3d}{\dfrac{d}{v1} + \dfrac{d}{v2} + \dfrac{d}{v3}} \\ & = & \dfrac{3{v}_{1}{v}_{2}{v}_{3}}{{v}_{1}{v}_{2} + {v}_{2}{v}_{3} + {v}_{3}{v}_{1}}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q:
The position-time graphs for two students $A$ and $B$ returning from the school to their homes are shown in figure.

(A) $A$ lives closer to the school

(B) $B$ lives closer to the school

(C) $A$ takes lesser time to reach home

(D) $A$ travels faster than $B$

(E) $B$ travels faster than $A$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the position time graph the velocity is found out by the slope of the line. The slope is given by& $\dfrac{{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}}{{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}$.

The slope of~$B$~is greater than~$A$. Hence, the velocity of~$B$~is greater than~$A$. As can be seen from the graph~${X}_{A} < {X}_{B}$. So~$A$~lives closer to the school and~${V}_{B} > {V}_{A}$. Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically up (taken as $+ z - axis$ ) from the ground. The correct momentum-height $( p - h )$ diagram is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If the ball was thrown with initial velocity $u$ , then its velocity at height $'h^{'}$ can be written as.
$v = \sqrt{u^{2} - 2gh}$
Its linear momentum, $p = mv = m\sqrt{u^{2} - 2gh}$
Or $p^{2} = m^{2}u^{2} - 2m^{2}gh$
The graph between $p \text{ and } h$ will be a parabola.
In motion when particle was going up, its velocity is positive and decreasing with height and so is the linear momentum. When it reaches the maximum height, the velocity and linear momentum will be zero. Again, it will start to fall back, the velocity and linear momentum will increase but will have negative value.

questions.q: Water droplets are coming from an open tap at a particular rate. The spacing between a droplet observed at ${4}^{th}$ second after its fall to the next droplet is $34 . 3m$. At what rate the droplets are coming from the tap ? (Take $g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In ${4}^{th}sec$,~${1}^{st}$ drop will travel~

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(9 . 8\right) \times \left(4\right)2 = 78 . 4m$

$∴ {2}^{nd}$ drop would have travelled

$⇒ 78 . 4 - 34 . 3 = 44 . 1m$

Time for~${2}^{nd}$ drop

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left(9 . 8\right)t^{2} = 44 . 1$

$t = 3sec$

$∴$ Each drop have time gap of $1sec$.

$∴ 1$ drop per second.

questions.q: If $t = \sqrt{x} + 4$, then \left(\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right)t = 4$ is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that& $t = \sqrt{x} + 4$

$⇒ x = \left(t - 4\right)2 = t^{2} - 8t + 16$

Differentiating the above equation with respect to time,

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2t - 8$

Putting the value of~$t = 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2 \times 4 - 8 = 0$

questions.q: A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position $x$ as a function of time $t$ is given as $x = \left(t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 20t + 15\right)m$. The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given the instantaneous position is

$x = t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 20t + 15 . . . \left(1\right)$

The velocity of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}v & = & \dfrac{dx}{dt}\\ & = & 3t^{2} - 12t + 20 . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$$

And, the acceleration of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}a & = & \dfrac{dv}{dt}\\ & = & 6t - 12 . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$$

When $a = 0$, it implies

$6t - 12 = 0 ⇒ t = 2s$

At $t = 2s$, the velocity can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}v & = & 3 ( 2{)}^{2} - 12 ( 2 ) + 20 \\ & = & 8ms^{- 1}\end{cases}$

questions.q: Two balls $A$ and $B$ are placed at the top of $180m$ tall tower. Ball $A$ is released from the top at $t = 0s$. Ball $B$ is thrown vertically down with an initial velocity $u$~at $t = 2s$. After a certain time, both balls meet $100m$ above the ground. Find the value of $u$~in $ms^{- 1}$. [use $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement covered by first ball,\left(180 - 100\right) = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^{2}$~ ~$⇒ t = 4s$

Now, the second body gets only, ${t}_{2} = 4 - 2 = 2s$.

Displacement covered by second will be same,

$80 = u \times 2 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times \left(2\right)2$

$⇒ u = \dfrac{80 - 20}{2} = 30ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: A body projected vertically upwards with a certain speed from the top of a tower reaches the ground in $t_1$. If it is projected vertically downwards from the same point with the same speed, it reaches the ground in $t_2$. Time required to reach the ground, if it is dropped from the top of the tower, is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{t}_1=\frac{\mathrm{u}+\sqrt{\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{gh}}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \mathrm{t}_2=\frac{-\mathrm{u}+\sqrt{\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{gh}}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \mathrm{t}=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2=\frac{\left(\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{gh}\right)-\mathrm{u}^2}{\mathrm{~g}^2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{gh}}{\mathrm{g}^2}=\mathrm{t}^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A horse rider covers half the distance with $5ms^{- 1}$ speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed $10ms^{- 1}$ for half the time and with speed $15ms^{- 1}$ for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is $\dfrac{x}{7}ms^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let total distance travelled by horse rider be& $2x$.

Now, the time taken to cover first half distance is~${t}_{AB} = \dfrac{x}{5}$

Second half distance $x$~between~$BC$~is covered in two parts,~$x = {d}_{1} + {d}_{2}$

here~${d}_{1}$~is the distance travelled with $10ms^{- 1}$~and~${d}_{2}$~is the distance travelled with $15ms^{- 1}$~in equal time intervals~$\dfrac{t}{2}$~each.

Then,~${d}_{1} = \dfrac{10t}{2}, {d}_{2} = \dfrac{15t}{2}$

Second half distance~$x = \dfrac{t}{2} ( 10 + 15 ) = \dfrac{25t}{2}$

Now, the mean speed of rider is~$v = \dfrac{2x}{\dfrac{x}{5} + \dfrac{2x}{25}} = \dfrac{2 \times 25}{5 + 2} = \dfrac{50}{7}ms^{- 1}$

Thus, the value of~$x = 50$.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of $19 . 6ms^{- 1}$ from the top of a tower. The ball strikes the ground after $6s$. The height from the ground up to which the ball can rise will be \left(\dfrac{k}{5}\right)m$. The value of $k$ is~_____ (use $g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial velocity of ball is& $u = 19 . 6ms^{- 1}$, final velocity~$v = 0$.

Using~$v = u + at$, here, acceleration~$a = - g$.

Time taken in upward motion above tower is~${t}_{a} = \dfrac{u}{g} = \dfrac{19 . 6}{9 . 8} = 2s$

Now, time taken from top most point to ground is~${t}_{d} = 6 - 2 = 4s$.

Or,~${t}_{d} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2{h}_\max}{g}}$~ ~ (Using~$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$)

$⇒ {h}_\max = \dfrac{16 \times 9 . 8}{2} = \dfrac{392}{5}m$.

Hence, the value of~$k = 392$.

questions.q: A particle initially at rest starts moving from reference point $x = 0$ along $x$-axis, with velocity $v$ that varies as $v = 4\sqrt{x}ms^{- 1}$. The acceleration of the particle is _____ $ms^{- 2}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: $v = 4\sqrt{x}$

Instantaneous acceleration of the particle can be written as, $a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$= \left(4\sqrt{x}\right) \times \left(4 \times \dfrac{1}{2}x^{- 1 / 2}\right) = 8ms^{- 2}$

questions.q: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement $x$ at any time $t$ is given by $x^2=1+t^2$. Its acceleration at any time $\mathrm{t}$ is $x^{-\mathrm{n}}$ where $\mathrm{n}=$ ___________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}^2=1+\mathrm{t}^2 \\ & 2 \mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{xv}=\mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{v} \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=1 \\ & \mathrm{x} \cdot \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{v}^2=1 \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{1-\mathrm{v}^2}{\mathrm{x}}=\frac{1-\mathrm{t}^2 / \mathrm{x}^2}{\mathrm{x}} \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^3}=\mathrmx^{-3}\end{aligned}$
